headline: High-risk prompt-injection and data-leakage pathways exist because LightAgent can browse, use MCP, and egress broadly while LightZero is a non-writing, no-egress peer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can run browsers, use MCP, and emit raw tool results; if LightZero consumes those outputs through a shared channel or copied artifacts, attacker-controlled content can steer instructions. LightZero itself has no ingestion surface, so the risk hinges on the pairwise bridge and LightAgent’s permissive I/O. Uncertainty about the bridge escalates to high.
conditions: IF LightAgent output is copied into LightZero prompts or game inputs without sanitization
IF an MCP server or shared workspace bridges LightAgent and LightZero
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of LightAgent outputs to LightZero
Add a strict allowlist/JSON schema validator on transferred content
Route any cross-agent text through a human review step
requires-engineering: isolate the agents in separate workspaces or containers
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and reject untrusted instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches conversations, memory, tool results, and workflow state and has broad network egress, so it can leak sensitive data if paired with any shared workspace or copied artifacts. LightZero has no filesystem write or network egress, which limits direct exfiltration from that side, but the pair still creates a one-way leakage path through LightAgent. The shared-data pathway is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF LightAgent receives secrets, conversations, or tool results that are later forwarded externally
IF both agents are given access to the same files or pasted transcripts
mitigations: Do not place secrets in any shared prompt or artifact
Turn off or redact LightAgent memory for paired runs
Use separate accounts and separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any outbound call
requires-engineering: restrict LightAgent egress to approved endpoints

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and use MCP, while LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-only or indirect coordination. Because LightZero lacks mutable surfaces, the pairwise conflict is limited and requires unusual orchestration to matter.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF LightAgent is wrapped with custom tooling that writes into LightZero-owned state
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only in paired runs
Avoid shared git or filesystem targets
Assign separate OAuth principals and API keys
requires-engineering: add resource locks around any shared mutable store

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool results, provenance metadata, and workflow state that LightZero could treat as input if an orchestrator chains them. LightZero is a game-playing agent with no documented verification or provenance checks here, so a bad upstream result can cascade into downstream decisions. The pathway exists in default-style chaining, but the blast radius is bounded by LightZero’s limited action surface.
conditions: IF LightZero consumes LightAgent outputs as authoritative state
IF no verification step checks provenance or correctness before downstream use
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require citations or structured evidence from LightAgent
Reject outputs that lack provenance metadata
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks
requires-engineering: separate planning from execution roles

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles conversations, memory, trace data, and secrets such as API keys, and it has broad network egress; LightZero is docs-only with no data classes touched. If the pair is used on regulated data, LightAgent can create residency or retention mismatches even though LightZero itself is not a direct compliance sink. The risk is driven by LightAgent’s handling of sensitive data, so only its profile is cited.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are processed through LightAgent
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared workflow
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through LightAgent
Minimize or disable logging and long-term memory
Use region-locked infrastructure for LightAgent
requires-engineering: add retention controls and deletion workflows
requires-engineering: document a DPA and data-flow map
